reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the formation of a dense HfO2 layer, Zr diffusion (~60 μm), and improved oxidation resistance for a Hf-coated VZrHfNbTa alloy, but the hypothesis extends these findings to a different substrate (high-entropy boride) and a molten aluminum corrosion environment, which are not addressed in the cited passages.
premises: Hf coating can be densified via hot-press sintering
Hf coating forms a dense HfO2 protective layer upon high-temperature oxidation
Zr diffusion creates a ~60 μm transition layer between Hf coating and substrate
HfO2 layer reduces oxidation/corrosion of the underlying alloy
Coating thickness of ~120 μm is achievable and effective
